# input: # French puts the decimal on "," and groups with U+202F, the narrow no-break
# space — not the ordinary one, and not the U+00A0 Ukrainian uses. Every
# formatted string below with four digits in it carries that character.
# And the fraction takes the *singular*: French's `one` category swallows
# every value below two, so it is "1,5 euro" here and "1,5 euros" in Spanish
# All three spaces are read back, so a user may type what the formatter
# printed, what their keyboard makes, or what a spreadsheet pasted.
# A currency with no minor unit still gets the narrow space.
# The vigesimal cardinal: ninety is "four-twenty-ten", one token joined by
# "en" and "vers" both introduce a target; multiply has a one-word form and
# a two-token one, and division only ever has the two-token one.
# The words French coined rather than borrowed. "livre" is also
# @smartput/mass's word for the pound, which is the same collision English
# has and is left standing for the same reason.
